attempts.goal:
Deliver a production SQLite 3.45+ migration script for this legacy help-desk database.
Existing schema, with foreign_keys=ON:
CREATE TABLE contacts(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  email TEXT, display_name TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE tickets(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, contact_id INTEGER NOT NULL
  REFERENCES contacts(id), subject TEXT NOT NULL);
Legacy contacts may duplicate an email within one tenant. Identity is tenant_id plus
lower(trim(email)), where trim removes ordinary ASCII spaces. Missing means email IS NULL or
trim(email)='': this includes empty strings and all-space strings. Preserve each missing
contact separately and normalize its email to NULL.
For each nonmissing duplicate identity, keep the row with least updated_at, breaking
ties by least id. Preserve that winner's id, display_name, tenant_id and updated_at.
Repoint every ticket to the winning contact before deleting losers. Preserve all ticket
IDs and subjects. Normalize retained nonmissing emails. Enforce this same normalized
uniqueness rule for FUTURE INSERTs and UPDATEs, without merging across tenants or making
missing emails unique. Add a unique index, without triggers or rebuilding the tables.
Never disable foreign-key enforcement.
The script must be atomic, including creation of the uniqueness constraint. If a statement
fails before COMMIT the transaction must still be rollbackable. Running the script twice
must produce the same data and constraints. Do not assume a particular row count or IDs.
Organize the work in dependent stages: have independent agents analyze data/FK invariants
and transaction/retry hazards; use their findings for an implementation agent; then have
a separate agent inspect that candidate for concrete counterexamples before delivery.
Correct any issue they identify within this run. You do not have a SQL execution tool,
so do not claim execution; deliver the script for an external SQLite evaluator.
Return ONLY JSON: {"marker":"EVAL_MIGRATION","sql":"complete script", "rationale":"..."}.

{"marker":"EVAL_MIGRATION","sql":"-- ============================================================================
-- contacts identity migration: dedupe by (tenant_id, lower(trim(email))),
-- repoint tickets, normalize emails, add future-enforcement unique index.
-- Target: SQLite 3.45+  |  No triggers, no table rebuild, FK enforcement ON.
--
-- CALLER CONTRACT:
--   * Run with no outer transaction open (autocommit), because this script
--     owns its transaction with BEGIN IMMEDIATE.
--   * On any error the script stops with the transaction still OPEN so the
--     caller can ROLLBACK; no implicit-commit statement is used anywhere.
--   * sqlite3 CLI users: enable ".bail on" so a failing statement stops the
--     script instead of falling through to COMMIT.
-- ============================================================================

PRAGMA busy_timeout = 10000;   -- non-transactional; only affects lock waiting
PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;      -- enforcement stays ON (never OFF)

BEGIN IMMEDIATE;               -- write lock up front: stable snapshot

-- Stage 0: retry safety - drop any leftover map from an interrupted attempt.
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS temp._mig_contacts_dedupe_map;

-- Stage 1: normalize MISSING emails to NULL.
--   missing := email IS NULL OR trim(email) = ''  (empty and all-space forms;
--   one-argument trim() strips only ordinary ASCII spaces U+0020).
--   Each missing contact keeps its own row; nothing is merged or made unique.
UPDATE contacts
   SET email = NULL
 WHERE email IS NOT NULL
   AND trim(email) = '';

-- Stage 2: normalize retained NONMISSING emails to lower(trim(email)).
--   Idempotent. Only the email column is written; id/display_name/tenant_id/
--   updated_at are never modified.
UPDATE contacts
   SET email = lower(trim(email))
 WHERE email IS NOT NULL
   AND email <> lower(trim(email));

-- Stage 3: freeze the loser -> winner map for each nonmissing identity.
--   identity = (tenant_id, lower(trim(email)))
--   winner   = greatest updated_at, ties broken by greatest id
--   (updated_at, id) is a total order (id is INTEGER PRIMARY KEY), so the
--   winner is unique per identity. Missing rows never enter the partition.
CREATE TEMP TABLE _mig_contacts_dedupe_map (
  loser_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  winner_id INTEGER NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO temp._mig_contacts_dedupe_map (loser_id, winner_id)
SELECT id, winner_id
  FROM (SELECT id,
               first_value(id) OVER (
                   PARTITION BY tenant_id, lower(trim(email))
                   ORDER BY updated_at DESC, id DESC) AS winner_id,
               row_number() OVER (
                   PARTITION BY tenant_id, lower(trim(email))
                   ORDER BY updated_at DESC, id DESC) AS rn
          FROM contacts
         WHERE email IS NOT NULL
           AND trim(email) <> '')
 WHERE rn > 1;

-- Stage 4: repoint every ticket that references a loser, BEFORE any delete.
--   tickets.contact_id is NOT NULL REFERENCES contacts(id) with no ON DELETE
--   action, enforced immediately while foreign_keys=ON.
--   Ticket id and subject are never written.
UPDATE tickets
   SET contact_id = (SELECT m.winner_id
                       FROM temp._mig_contacts_dedupe_map AS m
                      WHERE m.loser_id = tickets.contact_id)
 WHERE contact_id IN (SELECT loser_id FROM temp._mig_contacts_dedupe_map);

-- Stage 5: delete the losers (now unreferenced by tickets).
DELETE FROM contacts
 WHERE id IN (SELECT loser_id FROM temp._mig_contacts_dedupe_map);

-- Stage 6: drop the map (temp objects are not part of the delivered schema).
DROP TABLE temp._mig_contacts_dedupe_map;

-- Stage 7: uniqueness constraint for FUTURE INSERT/UPDATE, created inside the
--   same transaction (DDL is transactional in SQLite, so it rolls back too).
--   * key expression is identical to the dedupe identity above;
--   * partial predicate excludes missing emails (NULL, '', '   ', ...), so any
--     number of missing contacts may coexist per tenant;
--   * tenant_id leads the key, so tenants are never merged;
--   * drop+recreate guarantees the exact definition on every run.
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS main.contacts_tenant_email_norm_uq;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX main.contacts_tenant_email_norm_uq
    ON contacts (tenant_id, lower(trim(email)))
 WHERE email IS NOT NULL
   AND trim(email) <> '';

COMMIT;","rationale":"Single atomic transaction (BEGIN IMMEDIATE ... COMMIT) in strict dependency order: defensive drop of any leftover temp map, missing emails -> NULL, retained nonmissing emails -> lower(trim(email)), freeze loser->winner map in a TEMP table, repoint tickets, delete losers, drop temp map, drop+recreate the partial unique index, COMMIT. Tickets are repointed before any contact delete because tickets.contact_id is NOT NULL REFERENCES contacts(id) with no ON DELETE action and is enforced immediately while foreign_keys=ON; PRAGMA foreign_keys is only ever set to ON, never OFF, and appears before BEGIN. Winner selection uses first_value/row_number over PARTITION BY (tenant_id, lower(trim(email))) ORDER BY updated_at DESC, id DESC - a total order because id is the integer primary key - so only rn>1 rows are deleted; the winner's id, display_name, tenant_id and updated_at are never written, and ticket id/subject never appear in any SET list. The unique index key lower(trim(email)) is character-identical to the dedupe expression, scoped by tenant_id, and its partial predicate WHERE email IS NOT NULL AND trim(email) <> '' excludes NULL, empty and all-space emails so missing contacts stay non-unique; expression/partial indexes are maintained on INSERT and UPDATE, giving future enforcement with no triggers and no table rebuild. Idempotency: on a second run stages 1-2 match zero rows, the map is empty so the UPDATE/DELETE are no-ops, and the index is dropped and recreated with an identical definition, so data and constraints converge to the same state; no row counts or IDs are assumed. Atomicity: no VACUUM, no journal_mode change, no ATTACH, no implicit-commit statement; a failing statement leaves the transaction open and rollbackable, and no ROLLBACK is appended so the success path is not broken. RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTY (not verified by execution - no SQL execution tool was available in this run): (a) stock SQLite lower() is ASCII-only, so non-ASCII case variants (e.g. 'A-umlaut@x' vs its lowercase form) remain distinct - acceptable because dedupe and the index use the same expression; (b) one-argument trim() strips only U+0020, so tab/newline/NBSP padding is neither trimmed nor treated as missing; (c) without triggers, future rows are only checked for normalized uniqueness, not rewritten to lower(trim(email)) or NULL - legacy rows are normalized, future ''/'   ' values remain storable and non-unique; (d) the script assumes tickets is the only child table referencing contacts(id); any other child makes the DELETE fail loudly and the whole transaction roll back; (e) the script requires being started outside any open transaction (otherwise BEGIN IMMEDIATE errors); (f) pre-existing orphan tickets (possible only if the DB was loaded with FK off) are neither created nor repaired - PRAGMA foreign_key_check can be run by the evaluator afterwards."}
